role: Clemson University herpetologist and Duke consultant
stance_basis: paraphrased as providing factual survey data on salamander species without expressing support or opposition to the project
summary: Dr. Byron Ingram, a Clemson University herpetologist and Duke consultant, is cited as a source of herpetological survey data for the Bad Creek project area. He identified the Jordan's Salamander as common in the project area and listed the longtailed salamander and coal skink as rare, but no population estimates were made. His role is purely informational/scientific, with no expressed position for or against the project.
complaint_summary: Dr. Ingram is cited as listing the Jordan's Salamander (Plethodon jordani) as common in the project area, with no population estimate made, based on his herpetological survey conducted as a Duke consultant.
summary_quote: The Jordan's Salmander (Plethodon jordani) is listed by Dr. Byron Ingram, Clemson University herpetologist and one of Duke's consultants, as common in the project area, although no population estimate has been made (Applicant's Exhibit W).
